title: Microsoft Purview: inline DLP for prompts in Microsoft Foundry apps and agents
summary: Hold: the briefing says the policy-creation role is undocumented, although Microsoft's permissions reference identifies roles that create DLP policies. It also confuses a prompt not matching a rule with the prompt not being evaluated. The roadmap fields, pay-as-you-go requirement and printed PowerShell rule are supported.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans inline Purview DLP for prompts in Foundry-built apps and agents, with Purview enabled in Foundry.
claims.quote: With Purview enabled in Microsoft Foundry, Purview admins can setup inline DLP policies to prompts on Foundry built apps and agents to ensure data loss prevention of sensitive data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure, first bullet
claims.claim: A prompt containing data outside the policy's configured sensitive information types is not evaluated by that rule.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Foundry Purview blocked audit; opened ai-azure-foundry, developer/use-the-api and New-DlpComplianceRule. They describe evaluating content and applying rules on sensitive-type matches, not skipping evaluation because content does not match.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence with 'Learn documents blocking prompts based on sensitive information type matches; data outside the rule's configured types does not match that condition.' Retain the advice to review the configured types.

claims.claim: The documented app-specific policy does not automatically cover a different new Foundry app.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: PowerShell-only explanation; Open questions
claims.claim: No Purview portal creation path is documented for the Entra-registered app DLP policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Foundry DLP prompts create policy portal simulation Mode TestWithNotifications. Opened ai-azure-foundry and developer/use-the-api; the tutorial explicitly says the portal does not currently support creating DLP policies for Entra-registered applications.

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule with Policy, ContentContainsSensitiveInformation credit card number, and RestrictAccess UploadText Block is a documented app-DLP rule command.
claims.quote: -Policy "Test Entra DLP" -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @{Name = "credit card number"} ... -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="UploadText";value="Block"})

claims.claim: The DLP rule cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Example 4 creates the Entra-app-scoped policy with New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Locations and -EnforcementPlanes Application.
claims.quote: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name "Test Entra DLP" -Mode Enable -Locations $locations -EnforcementPlanes @("Application")

claims.claim: The Foundry portal route to Purview Data Security is Manage > Compliance > Data security and governance.
claims.quote: In the Foundry portal, select Manage > Compliance. ... Select the Data security and governance tab. ... Review the Powered by Microsoft Purview setting and the coverage indicators.
claims.fix: The route stops on the correct tab. Set the surface to 'Microsoft Foundry (new) portal' and extend the path to 'Manage > Compliance > Data security and governance > subscription > Powered by Microsoft Purview'. Retain the note that the setting shows the integration's enabled state.

claims.claim: The Data security and governance tab shows the Powered by Microsoft Purview enabled state for the selected subscription.
claims.quote: Select the subscription that you want to review. ... The Powered by Microsoft Purview setting shows the integration's enabled state.

claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Foundry Purview enable data security REST API toggle Microsoft.Security pricings extension. Opened Foundry Compliance, ai-onboarding and Microsoft.Security/pricings; the latter documents AIPromptEvidence, not a Purview enablement extension.
